      "body": "REPLACING A HAND-ROLLED HYPOTHESIS BY 'THE STANDARD ONE' CAN STRENGTHEN IT INTO FALSITY -- and the test is a REFUTATION probe at the intended object, not a satisfiability witness.\n\nMEASURED (pic-e, AJC 0095 r7). I built the vocabulary the project was missing (graded prime avoidance => FiniteInAffine for projective schemes, all sorry-free), then restated the seam's antecedent with IsProjective of the representing scheme in place of the elementary FiniteInAffine, and committed 'entirely in standard vocabulary, no condition invented in this project'. I ran THREE vacuity checks and all three PASSED: the new conjunct is satisfiable (Spec k is projective over itself), it is NOT free (exact? fails at an arbitrary object), and the new antecedent does not close hypothesis-free. A fresh-context audit then refuted it in one step.\n\nWHY THE CHECKS MISSED IT. Every one of them asks 'could this hypothesis hold SOMEWHERE?'. None asks 'does it hold AT THE OBJECT THE STATEMENT IS ABOUT?'. IsProjective over a field forces IsProper, hence UniversallyClosed, hence CompactSpace over the compact Spec k -- and Pic_{C/k} is a disjoint union over deg in Z, so it is not quasi-compact. The antecedent is FALSE at its only intended witness. Satisfiability elsewhere is exactly what makes that invisible.\n\nWORSE: my own project already had the refutation. Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean exists to record this as 'trap (c): a P -> Q whose antecedent is unsatisfiable in the intended setting', with the general theorems to check it -- and I had imported nothing from it.       "body": "RE-READING HEAD AT COMMIT TIME MAKES THE GUARD'S COMPARE-AND-SWAP PASS VACUOUSLY, AND THE PRIVATE INDEX DOES NOT COVER THIS\n\nMEASURED (janitor, pic-e 0095 r6, commit 3a511854e3). I ran the full I-1222 route -- fresh private index, read-tree HEAD, add only my 10 explicit paths, verified `diff --cached --name-status` listed exactly those 10, zero deletions. The commit still reverted another lane's file (`fc6de4ab54`, landed in the ~90s between my read-tree and my commit).\n\nTHE BUG IS ONE SHELL IDIOM. I set the guard's variable as `export ARCHON_COMMIT_BASE=$(\"$HORIZON_GIT\" rev-parse HEAD)` **in the commit step**, i.e. re-read HEAD instead of reusing the sha the index was seeded from. The hook then compares HEAD to itself and always passes. The guard is the only mechanism that catches a mid-pass HEAD advance -- the private index cannot, because read-tree snapshots a tree and a later commit is invisible to it. Capture BASE once, before read-tree, and reuse that literal.\n\nWHY IT LOOKED FINE: 10 staged paths, 10 verified, and the commit itself printed \"11 files changed\". Only reading EVERY path of the post-commit `diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat` caught the 11th. That is the check I-1222 demands and the one that earned its keep here.\n\nDamage was nil (both edits whitespace-only; I normalized the YAML across all three shas and the content is identical, and the owning lane then re-landed their wrapping as 73e93c577c). The lesson is the idiom, not the outcome.",

      "body": "AN 'ONLY PRODUCER IS FIELD-ONLY' CLAIM IS A CENSUS OF THE NAME YOU GUESSED, AND THE RING-LEVEL VERSION IS OFTEN LANDED UNDER A DIFFERENT MAP.\n\nMEASURED (pic-g 0096 r6, refuted by a fresh-context audit of my own file). Every clause was checkable and the conclusion was false: picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt (PicEtUnit.lean:161) supplies the same seam at an ARBITRARY test RING, no field, no section, no curve binder, with 11 call sites.\n\nWHY MY CENSUS MISSED IT, and this is the reusable part. I searched for producers of the SEAM'S NAME -- surjectivity of  -- because that is the shape of the conclusion I wanted. The landed producer is not about 's surjectivity at all: it is an AFFINE-CONSISTENCY lemma for a DIFFERENT map (relPicToPicEt) which happens to have the seam as its conclusion. A grep for 'unit_surjective' finds it never; a search for the CONCLUSION 'picEtAffineEquiv _ = PicEtAff.unit _ _' finds it first.\n\nSO THE RULE: when you are about to write 'the only producer is X, and X is too strong', search for the CONCLUSION you need, not for the strengthened statement whose name you have.       "body": "A THREE-LANE COMPOSITION IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY PER-ROW CHECK, AND THE ROWS WILL EACH TELL YOU THE WORK IS ELSEWHERE.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-e, AJC, 0095 r6). Three sorry-free theorems from three different lanes composed into a verbatim derivation of the project's central sorry from the classical pointed theorem: the unconditional finite-GALOIS-level rational point (Curve/), the picSharp->picEt transport (PicEtSubcanonical), and the lftFree descent step with hq and hcov already internal (PicEtGaloisQuotient). Eleven declarations, all axiom-clean, three commits.\n\nNO ROW MENTIONED THE OTHER TWO. The descent-assembly row listed FOUR open inputs; three were already discharged elsewhere. The seam docstring's own 'what remains' sentence listed three items, one of which was closed and one of which was DONE-AND-CALLED-REMAINING. Every row was individually plausible and internally consistent; the composition existed only across them.\n\nTHE MECHANISM, and why the usual checks miss it: each row is maintained by the lane that owns it, and a lane records what IT owes, not what another lane has since supplied. So a row goes stale in the CHEAP direction -- it schedules work that exists -- and nothing re-reads it, because a list of remaining obligations reads as self-criticism. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[unavoidable-is-not-geometric]], but distributed: no single sentence is wrong enough to notice.\n\nTHE CHECK THAT FINDS IT, and it is cheap: take the consumer theorem's LITERAL binder list -- #check the one a costing tells you to aim at -- and ask of EACH binder, separately, 'does a producer for exactly this exist at HEAD?'. Not 'is this gap open' (the row answers that) but 'is this BINDER discharged'. At the spelling that matters, seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree, three of four were gone and the fourth was an instance binder no row named. A four-item gap list and a one-item binder list were both accurate about different things.\n\nCOROLLARY, the part that cost me a withdrawal: after composing, price the RESULT against the WEAKEST antecedent your proof consumes, not the shape the hand-off wants. My first antecedent carried IsSeparated, which is provably free from the conclusion's own representation, and a reduction whose antecedent contains a free conjunct misreports exactly the number it exists to report. Related: [[price-the-consumer-carrier]], [[audit-the-goals-antecedents-not-the-lemmas]].",

      "body": "A \"TRAP, MEASURED -- DO NOT ROUTE VIA X\" NOTE IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE FALSE CLAIM A LANE CAN SHIP, AND THE CHEAPEST TEST IS TO GREP WHETHER A SIBLING FILE ALREADY DOES X.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (AJCR, pic-c 0092 r5, Pic0VanishingFieldGenusZero.lean:33-38). A lane recorded, in a file header, a commit message, and a direct message to another lane: \"going through chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle C K produces the same object under a different Over instance, and the two chi terms DO NOT UNIFY -- measured\". It reads like exactly the kind of hard-won spelling fact worth broadcasting, and the receiving lane accepted it.\n\nIt is false. The bundled route closes with one `change` to the bundled spelling followed by `simpa`, at DEFAULT heartbeats. What had been measured was that one `simpa` failed without the `change`, i.e. a fact about a tactic invocation, published as a fact about two objects.\n\nTHE TEST THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT COST ONE GREP. A sibling lane had written the prohibited proof, at a concrete curve, in the same hour, and it was at HEAD and root-imported: Curve/P1DegreeZeroTrivial.lean:83-99 uses chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle with the same change + simpa. So before publishing \"route X does not work\", grep the tree for X: a live use site refutes the prohibition outright, and its presence in a file you did not write is more likely than it feels, because a prohibition is usually discovered exactly when two lanes are on the same object.\n\nWHY IT IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY OVERCLAIM. A positive overclaim gets tested when someone tries to use the result. A prohibition is never tested -- its whole function is to stop people trying -- so it can survive indefinitely and it forecloses a cheap route for every later round. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[exculpatory-sentence-is-a-claim]], but with a longer half-life.\n\nCOROLLARY, same round, same file: unexplained `set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000` raises with a comment asserting the default is exceeded. Copying both files verbatim with the default budget: EXIT=0, all six declarations. A budget raise is a claim too, and re-running the file at the default is a 40-second check.",

      "body": "LIVE: A STALE ZERO-BYTE index.lock IS HANGING plain git commit ON THE SHARED LEDGER. Read if a commit of yours times out with no output.\n\nMEASURED (pic-g, 0096 r3): .archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git/index.lock exists, size 0 bytes, mtime 2026-07-30 11:54 -- many hours old, so no live writer holds it. Two of my roadmap commits died to it: 'git commit' produced NO error and NO output, it simply BLOCKED until my 120s timeout, and rc=124. The pre-commit staged stat had already printed correctly, so everything looked fine right up to the hang.\n\nWHY IT IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN ANNOYING: a timed-out commit DOES NOT LAND, and the failure is silent. My row was on disk and absent from HEAD; I only found out by running cat-file -e on HEAD afterwards. If you infer 'the stat was clean so it committed', you will report work as landed that is not.\n\nTHE FIX THAT WORKED, and it needs no lock at all: build the tree in a private index and write the commit with plumbing.\n  export GIT_INDEX_FILE=/tmp/mine.idx; rm -f $GIT_INDEX_FILE\n  OLD=$(git rev-parse HEAD); git read-tree $OLD; git add <your explicit paths>\n  git diff --cached --name-status $OLD      # confirm ONLY your paths\n  TREE=$(git write-tree)\n  NEW=$(printf '%s\\n' \"msg...\" | git commit-tree $TREE -p $OLD)\n  git update-ref refs/heads/main $NEW $OLD  # compare-and-swap: fails if HEAD moved\n  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat                # and READ IT\nupdate-ref with the OLD sha is a genuine compare-and-swap, so it is safe against the race I-1222 describes AND does not touch index.lock. Landed my row as 671e4c657a this way after two plain-commit timeouts.\n\nI did NOT delete the lock file: other lanes are live and I-1504 warns against removing it blind. The plumbing route makes deleting it unnecessary.",

      "body": "A \"STRICTLY WEAKER REDUCTION\" CAN BE INTERDERIVABLE AT THE VERY SITE YOU RECOMMEND IT FOR -- and neither endpoint of the abstract statement shows it.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (AJC, Picard/DivSupportQuasiFinite.lean, run 0095 r5, three commits in ~20 minutes). A lane landed three reductions of one instance binder and ranked them by hypothesis strength: two point-set forms needing HasProperSupport, and a fibrewise form (via mathlib's LocallyQuasiFinite.of_fiberToSpecResidueField) advertised as \"STRICTLY WEAKER in hypotheses ... it applies to a module with no properness assumption whatever\". A whole commit plus two docstring sections tell a future producer to aim at the fibrewise one.\n\nThe strength ordering is TRUE for an arbitrary module. It is EMPTY at the recommended site. Probed both directions AT A DivFamily, where properSupport is a structure field:\n- fibrewise antecedent gives the point-set antecedent (compose the new of_fibers with the new iff);\n- point-set antecedent gives the fibrewise one (of_finite_preimage_singleton, then the ambient IsProper from the field, then inferInstance per fibre).\nBoth close. So at the only place a producer will ever stand, the three differently-priced antecedents are ONE antecedent, and the third commit bought a spelling.\n\nTHE GENERALISABLE TELL: a hypothesis-strength claim is about a lemma's BINDER LIST; the advice built on it is about a SITE. Whenever the site supplies the binder that separates the forms -- here properSupport as a field -- the separation collapses there, and the collapse is invisible from either end of the abstract statement.       "body": "\"MY NEW THEOREM SUBSUMES THE OLD ONE\" IS A TWO-DIRECTION CLAIM, AND A DISCHARGE PINS A BINDER THE OLD LEMMA LEFT FREE.\n\nMEASURED (reviewer, AJC run 0095 r2, auditing pic-e's isInvariantMatch_canonical). One example with an explicit rho binder refutes it in one line: Type mismatch, the pinned action against rho.\n\nTHE SHAPE, which recurs whenever a hypothesis is discharged rather than supplied: discharging works by CHOOSING the object the hypothesis was quantified over. That trades generality in that binder for freedom in the others. So the new theorem is more general in the extension and LESS general in the action, i.e. incomparable -- and \"subsumes\" is the one word that cannot be true.\n\nTHE CHECK, cheap and skipped every time: write the old lemma's statement, close it with the new theorem, and see it fail.       "body": "A PREDICATE MATCH BETWEEN TWO READINGS OF AN OBJECT YOUR OWN DEFINITION BUILT IS NATURALITY, NOT GEOMETRY.\n\nMEASURED (pic-e, AJC run 0095 r2, isInvariantMatch_canonical, Picard/PicEtInvariantMatch.lean, build EXIT=0 zero sorries). Campaign G1's remaining debt on the etale-descent route was IsInvariantMatch: that a class's representing morphism being Gal-EQUIVARIANT agrees with the class being Gal-INVARIANT. Four roadmap rows, five files and one whole hypothesis slot treated it as an input; my own r1 file introduced it as a named hypothesis and priced 'a model at a nontrivial automorphism' as the open question.\n\nIt is FREE at every extension, with no finiteness, separability or IsGalois binder.\n\nTHE TELL, which is what generalises: the two predicates are stated about the SAME object, and one side's action was DEFINED by transporting the other side's functor action along the representation (twistMor := rep.homEquiv.symm of galoisActionPicEt at the universal class). So the match cannot be independent content -- applying rep.homEquiv to one side and using NATURALITY of the transported transformation at phi.op turns it into the other. Three formal steps, zero geometry.\n\nTHE QUESTION NOBODY ASKED for four rounds: what is the action DEFINED AS? Everyone read semilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy as 'the action is free, good' and then continued pricing a match against it as if the action were arbitrary. A hypothesis about two objects is suspect the moment one of them is constructed from the other.\n\nSO THE CHECK, before pricing any 'these two predicates agree' obligation: find the DEFINITION of each side's structure. If either is built by transporting a natural transformation along an equivalence, try naturality at the morphism the predicate quantifies over before budgeting anything. And distinguish this from the genuinely-open sibling: hcov, on the same route, is a COVERING statement about two objects neither of which is defined from the other, and it did not fall to this.",

      "body": "A --summary WRITE IS A SILENT DESTRUCTIVE EDIT, AND THE TOOL'S OWN OUTPUT CANNOT SHOW IT. Check the commit STAT, not the command's success line.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-c, AJCR 0092 r1). I claimed a row with roadmap set --owner --status --summary. The CLI printed 'Updated roadmap item' and nothing else. The commit stat then read 46 insertions / 117 DELETIONS. --summary REPLACES; the 117 lines were review-ajcr's rank-elevation analysis of that exact fork, TWO author self-retractions inside it, and the row's stated live target. I had read the row earlier in the session, but through roadmap list, which truncates -- so I never saw the body I was about to overwrite.\n\nWHY THE EXISTING LESSONS DO NOT COVER IT. The workspace has roadmap-yaml-edit-reverts-owner (a prose edit writing a stale OWNER over a live claim) and several items about staged deletions of other lanes' FILES. This is neither: the owner field was fine, no file was staged D, the write was to a row I legitimately hold, and the loss was entirely inside one YAML string. Every file-level check passes.\n\nTHE RULE, cheap and it is the only one that works. After any roadmap set --summary, read the commit stat. A deletion count above a handful means you replaced prose you never read. Recover with git show <commit>^:<path>, merge the prior summary verbatim, append yours behind a marker saying what happened, and re-verify a distinctive phrase from the old text is present.\n\nTHE SHARPER POINT. The destroyed text contained a retraction whose lesson was 'a probe with the hypothesis as a BINDER measures the conversion, so the control looks audited' -- i.e. I deleted a warning about exactly the class of error a reviewer had just caught me making elsewhere in the same session. Board prose is where a lane's corrections live, and it is the least protected thing in the workspace: no build breaks, no test fails, no file appears deleted.",

     9	/-!
    10	# Degree slices of the relative-divisor functor + the degree-refined Abel map
    11	
    12	Campaign milestones **D1'** (degree-`d` divisor functor `DivFunctorDeg`, clopen
    13	degree decomposition, base-change stability of the fibre degree) and **A2**
    14	(degree-refined Abel map `abelDeg`) of the `instHasPicScheme` campaign
    15	(`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`), on top of the landed divisor
    16	functor `Scheme.DivFunctor` (Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §3 Def. `df:div`;
    17	`Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean`).
    18	
    19	## The fibre degree
    20	
    21	For a family of relative effective divisors `x : DivFamily π T` (the quotient
    22	encoding: `q : O_{X_T} ↠ F = O_D` with invertible kernel ideal `I_D = ker q`),
    23	the **fibre degree** at `t : T` is
    24	
    25	  `x.fiberDeg t := dim_{κ(t)} Γ(D_t, O_{D_t}) = dim_{κ(t)} Γ((X_T)_t, F_t)`,
    26	
    27	Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`'s degree of the fibre divisor `D_t ⊆ X_t` — the
    28	`H⁰`-only, cohomology-free rank.
    29	
    30	**AUDIT (encoding choice, D1').** The campaign phrase "rank-`d` of the
    31	finite-flat pushforward of `O_D`" is realized by its *pointwise shadow*: the
    32	in-tree substrate has no `q_* O_D`-as-locally-free-object (that is exactly the
    33	B3 rigid-pushforward engine, unbuilt), and for a finite flat family the rank of
    34	the pushforward at `t` *equals* `dim_{κ(t)} Γ(D_t, O_{D_t})` (pushforward along
    35	an affine morphism is exact and commutes with base change).  The fibre-section
    36	form is honest at full generality (any `π`, any `T`; `Module.finrank` junk
    37	value `0` if the fibre sections are infinite-dimensional, which does not occur
    38	for divisor fibres in the relative-curve regime) and is what Kleiman's
    39	`deg D_t` means.  When B3 lands, `q_* O_D` is locally free of rank
    40	`fiberDeg` and the two vocabularies fuse.
    41	
    42	**AUDIT (base change, D1').** `fiberDeg` is stable under arbitrary base change
    43	`ψ : T' ⟶ T` (`fiberDeg_pullbackAlong`): the fibre of `X_{T'}/T'` at `t'` is
    44	the base change of the fibre of `X_T/T` at `t = ψ(t')` along the residue
    45	extension `κ(t) → κ(t')`, and `H⁰` of a finitely presented module with proper
    46	support commutes with base field extension (Stacks 02KH at `i = 0`).  This is
    47	proved **axiom-clean** from the twist-free Γ-fibre core
    48	`Scheme.finrank_gammaTop_baseChange_of_hasProperSupport`
    49	(`Picard/SchematicSupport.lean`) — NOT from the twisted engine
    50	`Scheme.hilbertFunction_quotBaseMap` (`Picard/QuotFunctorDef.lean`), which
    51	still rests on the sorried tensor–pullback leaf
    52	`Modules.pullbackTensorMap_isIso`.  At `m = 0` no twist is needed, so the
    53	degree lane stays sorry-free (recon correction to the campaign plan's
    54	"the 02KE/02KH engine is landed" — only its untwisted core is).
    55	
    56	## The clopen degree decomposition — honest form
    57	
    58	**AUDIT (coproduct pin, D1').** The naive presheaf-level statement
    59	"`DivFunctor = ⨿_d DivFunctorDeg d`" is FALSE: on a disconnected `T` a family
    60	with non-constant fibre degree lies in no degree piece, and at `T = ∅` every
    61	piece contains the (unique) empty family, so the pieces are not disjoint.  The
    62	honest pins delivered here are:
    63	
    64	* every `T`-point decomposes `T` into clopen constant-degree pieces
    65	  (`DivFamily.degLocus`, `DivFamily.hasFiberDeg_pullbackAlong_degLocusHom`,
    66	  `DivFamily.iSup_degLocus`, `DivFamily.degLocus_disjoint`) — this is the form
    67	  the coproduct assembly `G4` (`hom_sigma_decompose`) consumes;
    68	* on a nonempty preconnected `T` the canonical comparison
    69	  `Σ_d (DivFunctorDeg π d)(T) → DivFunctor π (T)` is a bijection
    70	  (`divFunctorDeg_sigma_bijective`);
    71	* degree pieces of a common class agree (`DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg.unique`,
    72	  nonempty `T`).
    73	
    74	The only non-formal input is **Zariski-local constancy of the fibre degree**.
    75	This is TRUE in the campaign regime (relative curve: `D → T` is
    76	proper + quasi-finite, hence finite, and a finitely presented `T`-flat module
    77	with finite support has finite locally free pushforward — Mumford, *Abelian
    78	Varieties* II §5; Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`) but is NOT derivable from the
    79	current in-tree substrate (it needs the finite/rank half of the B3 pushforward
    80	engine plus `D_t` finite from relative dimension 1).  Following the house gate
    81	pattern (`HasPicScheme`), it is pinned as the instance-free Prop-class
    82	`HasLocallyConstantDivDeg C` at the AJC curve regime, and every decomposition
    83	statement is ALSO provided in hypothesis-parametrized form (an explicit
    84	`IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg` argument), so the eventual discharge is a
    85	one-line instance.  We deliberately do NOT state the gate for general `π`:
    86	for relative dimension `≥ 2` the fibre rank of `O_{D_t}` can jump (only `χ` is
    87	locally constant), which is why Kleiman filters `Div` by Hilbert polynomials in
    88	general and by the degree only over curves.
    89	
    90	## The degree ledger and the Abel-map sign (A2)
    91	
    92	**Sign convention (audit item 7-half).** The Abel map is
    93	`abelMapWitness C = abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`, i.e.
    94	
    95	  `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[ker q]`  —
    96	
    97	a divisor family maps to the *negative* of the class of its ideal sheaf
    98	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:461`).  The degree-refined Abel map
    99	`abelDeg C d : divFunctorDeg C d ⟶ picSharp C` is the restriction of
   100	`abelMapWitness` along the degree-`d` inclusion; its defining property is
   101	`abelDeg_app_mk`.  It deliberately lands in `picSharp C` — carving out
   102	`picSharpDeg C d` is milestone B4, not this file.
   103	
   104	**AUDIT (degree-coherence vocabulary, A2).** "The ideal sheaf `ker q` of a
   105	rank-`d` family has fibre degree `−d`" is stated in the **rank (colength)
   106	vocabulary** — the strongest honestly-provable form today: the χ-ledger
   107	(`deg = χ(I) − χ(O)`, campaign P3) is unbuilt, and the adelic
   108	`RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor` degree cannot yet be attached to the sheaf-theoretic
   109	line bundle `ker q` on a family fibre (that needs the `M ≅ O(div s)`
   110	regular-section bricks, also P3).  What IS proved, per fibre `t`:
   111	
   112	* the ideal restricts to the fibre: the kernel–pullback comparison
   113	  `(I_D)_t ≅ ker(q_t)` is an isomorphism (`DivFamily.fiberKernelIso`) and the
   114	  fibre ideal inclusion `(I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t}` stays monic
   115	  (`DivFamily.mono_fiber_kernel_ι`) with `(I_D)_t` invertible
   116	  (`DivFamily.isLocallyTrivial_fiber_kernel`) — `D_t ⊆ X_t` is an honest
   117	  effective Cartier divisor (Kleiman §3, note after Def. `df:div`);
   118	* its colength is the degree: `O_{X_t}/(I_D)_t ≅ (O_D)_t`
   119	  (`DivFamily.fiberCokernelIso`), so
   120	  `dim_{κ(t)} Γ(coker((I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t})) = fiberDeg x t = d`
   121	  (`DivFamily.fiberDeg_eq_finrank_fiber_cokernel`,
   122	  `DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg.finrank_fiber_cokernel`).
   123	
   124	In χ-ledger terms this is exactly `deg_t(ker q) = χ(I_t) − χ(O_{X_t}) = −d`;
   125	the translation becomes a theorem once P3 lands.
   126

   133	Stacks 02KH (`i = 0`) for the base-change core.

   149	
   150	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
   151	/-- **Transport of the fibre-section dimension along an isomorphism of fibre
   152	modules.**  An isomorphism of sheaves of modules on the scheme-theoretic fibre
   153	`π₀.fiber s` induces a `κ(s)`-linear equivalence on global sections
   154	(evaluation at `⊤` is functorial, and the `κ(s)`-scalar action factors through
   155	`Scheme.Hom.fiberResidueMap`), so the `κ(s)`-dimensions agree.  Twist-free
   156	sibling of `Scheme.hilbertFunction_eq_finrank_of_iso`
   157	(`Picard/QuotFunctorDef.lean`), serving the degree lane where no tensor
   158	operations may enter. -/
   159	lemma finrank_fiberSections_eq_of_iso {W B : Scheme.{u}} (π₀ : W ⟶ B) (s : B)
   160	    {G G' : (π₀.fiber s).Modules} (e : G ≅ G') :
   161	    (letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G
   162	     Module.finrank (B.residueField s) Γ(G, ⊤))
   163	      = (letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G'
   164	         Module.finrank (B.residueField s) Γ(G', ⊤)) := by
   165	  letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G
   166	  letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G'
   167	  have γe := ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules (π₀.fiber s) ⋙
   168	    PresheafOfModules.evaluation (π₀.fiber s).ringCatSheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)).mapIso
   169	      e).toLinearEquiv
   170	  exact LinearEquiv.finrank_eq
   171	    { toFun := γe
   172	      map_add' := γe.map_add
   173	      map_smul' := fun c x => γe.map_smul ((π₀.fiberResidueMap s).hom c) x
   174	      invFun := γe.symm
   175	      left_inv := γe.left_inv
   176	      right_inv := γe.right_inv }

   178	/-! ## §1. The fibre degree of a family of relative effective divisors -/
   179	
   180	namespace DivFamily
   181	
   182	variable {π : X ⟶ S}
   183	
   184	/-- The **fibre degree** of a family of relative effective divisors
   185	`x : DivFamily π T` at a point `t : T` (Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`):
   186	
   187	  `deg D_t := dim_{κ(t)} Γ(D_t, O_{D_t}) = dim_{κ(t)} Γ((X_T)_t, F_t)`,
   188	
   189	the `κ(t)`-dimension of the global sections of the restriction of the divisor
   190	structure sheaf `F = O_D` to the scheme-theoretic fibre `(X_T)_t`.  This is
   191	the pointwise shadow of "rank of the finite-flat pushforward `q_* O_D`" (equal
   192	to it whenever the pushforward exists as a locally free module, i.e. in the
   193	relative-curve regime once the B3 engine lands; see the module docstring
   194	audit).  `Module.finrank` junk value `0` in the infinite-dimensional case. -/
   195	noncomputable def fiberDeg {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
   196	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) : ℕ :=
   197	  letI := (pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberSectionsModule t
   198	    ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t x.F)
   199	  Module.finrank (T.left.residueField t)
   200	    Γ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t x.F, ⊤)
   201	
   202	/-- **The fibre degree is well defined on divisor classes**: equivalent
   203	families (`DivFamily.Rel`, i.e. same divisor `ker q = ker q'`) have equal
   204	fibre degrees — the target isomorphism restricts to each fibre and transports
   205	the section dimension. -/
   206	theorem Rel.fiberDeg_eq {T : Over S} {x y : DivFamily π T} (h : x.Rel y)
   207	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) : x.fiberDeg t = y.fiberDeg t := by
   208	  obtain ⟨f, -⟩ := h
   209	  exact finrank_fiberSections_eq_of_iso (pullback.snd π T.hom) t
   210	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).mapIso f)
   211	
   212	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
   213	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
   214	-- Heartbeat headroom: instantiating the Γ-fibre base-change core provisions
   215	-- pullback/pushforward and field instances under binders, as in the sibling
   216	-- engines of `QuotFunctorDef`.
   217	/-- **The fibre degree is stable under base change** (Stacks 02KH at `i = 0`;
   218	Kleiman §3, functoriality of `Div`): for `ψ : T' ⟶ T` and `t' : T'` over
   219	`t := ψ(t')`, the fibre degree of the pulled-back family at `t'` equals the
   220	fibre degree of `x` at `t`.
   221	
   222	Route (all inputs axiom-clean): the fibre of `X_{T'}/T'` at `t'` is the base
   223	change of the fibre of `X_T/T` at `t` along `Spec κ(t') → Spec κ(t)`
   224	(`Scheme.isPullback_fiberBaseChange`, the `quotBaseSquare`/residue-field
   225	pasting); the two fibre restrictions of `F` are matched by pseudofunctor
   226	coherence (`Scheme.pullbackSquareIso`); proper support of `F/T` restricts to
   227	the fibre (`Modules.HasProperSupport.of_isPullback` on Mathlib's fibre
   228	square); and the twist-free Γ-fibre flat base-change core
   229	`Scheme.finrank_gammaTop_baseChange_of_hasProperSupport`
   230	(`Picard/SchematicSupport.lean` — support descent `G ≅ i_* i^* G` + the
   231	CLOSED 02KE heart) transports the dimension across the residue extension.
   232	No tensor operations enter, so — unlike the twisted engine
   233	`hilbertFunction_quotBaseMap` — this consumes no sorried leaf. -/
   234	theorem fiberDeg_pullbackAlong {T T' : Over S} (ψ : T' ⟶ T) (x : DivFamily π T)
   235	    (t' : (T'.left : Scheme.{u})) :
   236	    (x.pullbackAlong ψ).fiberDeg t' = x.fiberDeg (ψ.left.base t') := by
   237	  haveI hFqc : x.F.IsQuasicoherent := letI := x.isFinitePresentation; inferInstance
   238	  haveI : ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule (ψ.left.base t') x.F).IsQuasicoherent :=
   239	    pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom _ x.F hFqc
   240	  have hpsFt : Modules.HasProperSupport
   241	      ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberToSpecResidueField (ψ.left.base t'))
   242	      ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule (ψ.left.base t') x.F) :=
   243	    Modules.HasProperSupport.of_isPullback
   244	      (IsPullback.of_hasPullback (pullback.snd π T.hom)
   245	        (T.left.fromSpecResidueField (ψ.left.base t')))
   246	      x.F x.isFinitePresentation x.properSupport
   247	  have eF : (pullback.snd π T'.hom).fiberModule t'
   248	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).obj x.F)
   249	      ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback (fiberBaseChange π ψ t')).obj
   250	          ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule (ψ.left.base t') x.F) :=
   251	    pullbackSquareIso (fiberBaseChange_fiberι π ψ t').symm x.F
   252	  exact (finrank_fiberSections_eq_of_iso (pullback.snd π T'.hom) t' eF).trans
   253	    (Scheme.finrank_gammaTop_baseChange_of_hasProperSupport
   254	      (Field.toIsField (T.left.residueField (ψ.left.base t')))
   255	      (Field.toIsField (T'.left.residueField t'))
   256	      (isPullback_fiberBaseChange π ψ t')
   257	      ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule (ψ.left.base t') x.F) hpsFt)
   258	
   259	/-! ## §2. The fibre of the ideal sheaf — Cartier fibres and the degree ledger
   260	
   261	The `[D] ↦ -[ker q]` sign convention of the Abel map (module docstring) is
   262	anchored fibrewise: on every fibre `X_t` of the family, the ideal sheaf
   263	restricts to an honest invertible ideal `(I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t}` cutting out the
   264	fibre divisor `D_t`, and its colength `dim_{κ(t)} Γ(O_{X_t}/(I_D)_t)` is
   265	exactly the fibre degree.  In χ-ledger terms (campaign P3, unbuilt):
   266	`deg_t(ker q) = χ((I_D)_t) − χ(O_{X_t}) = −deg D_t = −d` for a degree-`d`
   267	family. -/
   268	
   269	/-- **The kernel ideal restricts to an invertible ideal on every fibre**
   270	(Kleiman §3, note after Def. `df:div`, specialised to the fibre inclusion):
   271	the kernel of the fibre restriction `q_t` of the quotient map is locally
   272	trivial of rank one.  Instantiation of the divisor base-change theorem
   273	`Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial`
   274	(`lem:relative_divisor_base_change`) at Mathlib's fibre square. -/
   275	theorem isLocallyTrivial_fiber_kernel {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
   276	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
   277	    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial (Limits.kernel
   278	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).map x.q)) :=
   279	  Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial
   280	    (IsPullback.of_hasPullback (pullback.snd π T.hom)
   281	      (T.left.fromSpecResidueField t)) x.q x.epi
   282	    (pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom (pullback.fst π T.hom)
   283	      (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) inferInstance)
   284	    x.isFinitePresentation x.flat x.kerLocallyTrivial

   287	— the fibre divisor `D_t ⊆ X_t` is an effective Cartier divisor (its ideal is
   288	an invertible subsheaf, not merely an invertible quotient-kernel).  This is
   289	the flat-base-change monomorphism `Modules.mono_pullback_map_kernel_ι`
   290	(Stacks 00HL affine-locally) at the fibre square: `T`-flatness of `O_D` is
   291	what forbids the ideal from degenerating on special fibres. -/
   292	theorem mono_fiber_kernel_ι {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
   293	    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :

    12	/-!
    13	# The relative-divisor functor `Div_{X/S}` (real definition)
    14	
    15	This file constructs the relative-effective-divisor functor
    16	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.DivFunctor π : (Sch/S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1)` of Kleiman,
    17	"The Picard scheme", §3 (Def. `df:red` + Def. `df:div`; FGA Explained Ch. 9,
    18	arXiv:math/0504020), the source of the Abel map of the A.2.c FGA assembly
    19	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, whose `divFunctor` carrier this file
    20	makes real).
    21	
    22	## Encoding decision (quotient encoding)
    23	
    24	Kleiman §3 Def. `df:red`/`df:div`: a *relative effective divisor* on `X_T/T`
    25	is a closed subscheme `D ⊆ X_T` whose ideal `I` is **invertible** and which is
    26	**`T`-flat**; `Div_{X/S}(T)` is the set of such `D`.  We encode a divisor by
    27	its structure-sheaf quotient — the same encoding by which `Div ⊆ Hilb =
    28	Quot_{O}` sits inside the Quot functor (Kleiman §3 Thm. `th:repDiv`): a
    29	`DivFamily π T` is a `Scheme.QuotFamily`-shaped structure with `E` the unit
    30	module `O_X` (so `q : O_{X_T} ⟶ F` up to the canonical isomorphism
    31	`(pr₁)^* O_X ≅ O_{X_T}`; we state the source of `q` verbatim as the pullback
    32	of the unit, exactly as `QuotFamily` does for a general `E`, so that the whole
    33	pullback/functoriality skeleton of `QuotFunctorDef.lean` is reusable), and the
    34	**divisor condition** is: the kernel ideal `I = ker q` is invertible, encoded
    35	by the project-side line-bundle predicate
    36	`Scheme.LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial (kernel q)` (locally trivial of rank one,
    37	Stacks 01HK — the same predicate that carves the line bundles out of
    38	`Scheme.Modules` in `Picard/LineBundlePullback.lean`).  Between the two
    39	candidate encodings of invertibility (a bundled mono `ι : I ⟶ O` with a
    40	cokernel identification, versus the predicate on the categorical kernel) we
    41	choose the **kernel predicate**: `X.Modules` is abelian, so `ker q` is
    42	available functorially with no extra data fields, the equivalence relation on
    43	families stays literally that of the Quot functor (`ker q = ker q'` — no
    44	well-definedness burden for extra fields), and invertibility-of-an-object is
    45	exactly what `IsLocallyTrivial` and its proved pullback-stability
    46	(`IsLocallyTrivial.pullback`, Stacks 01HH) speak about.
    47	
    48	Two families are equivalent iff an isomorphism of the targets commutes with
    49	the quotient maps — equivalently `ker q = ker q'` as subobjects of `O_{X_T}`,
    50	i.e. the two quotients cut out the same closed subscheme `D`.  The value
    51	`DivFunctor π |_T` is the quotient by this relation, so it is Kleiman's *set*
    52	of relative effective divisors on `X_T/T`, not a groupoid of quotients.
    53	
    54	Faithfulness notes (Kleiman §3):
    55	
    56	* the fields `isFinitePresentation` and `properSupport` do not shrink the set
    57	  of divisors in the intended regime: `F = O_D = coker(I ⟶ O)` with `I`
    58	  invertible is automatically finitely presented, and for the FGA
    59	  instantiation (`π` proper, e.g. the curve `C/k`) the schematic support `D`
    60	  is a closed subscheme of the `T`-proper `X_T`, hence automatically proper
    61	  over `T`.  They are included to keep the family shape identical to
    62	  `QuotFamily` (Div sits inside Hilb) and to reuse its base-change lemmas
    63	  verbatim;
    64	* there is **no Hilbert-polynomial field**: Kleiman's `Div_{X/S}` (`df:div`)
    65	  is not filtered by `Φ` — the degree decomposition `Div = ∐_m Div^m`
    66	  (Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`) is a later, separate refinement;
    67	* no hypotheses on `π` are needed for the *functor* (Kleiman `df:div` imposes
    68	  none; projectivity/flatness enter only in the representability theorem
    69	  `th:repDiv`, which is not stated in this file).
    70	
    71	## Base-change well-definedness
    72	
    73	The pullback action reuses the `QuotFamily` base-change lemmas for the shared
    74	fields (finite presentation: `Modules.pullback_isFinitePresentation`, proved;
    75	flatness: `CoherentSheafFlat.of_isPullback`, proved; proper support:
    76	`Modules.HasProperSupport.of_isPullback`, proved in
    77	`Picard/QuotSupportBaseChange.lean`) and needs exactly one new fact for the
    78	divisor condition, proved in this file as the theorem
    79	`Scheme.Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial` (blueprint
    80	`lem:relative_divisor_base_change`): the kernel of the pulled-back quotient
    81	is the pullback of the kernel — because `0 → I → O → O_D → 0` stays exact
    82	after base change, `Tor_1` against the `T`-flat `O_D` vanishing (Kleiman §3,
    83	functoriality note after `df:div`: "Since `D` is `T`-flat, `p_{X_T}^* I`
    84	equals the ideal of `D_{T'}`") — and pullback preserves invertibility
    85	(`IsLocallyTrivial.pullback`, Stacks 01HH).  The theorem carries a
    86	quasi-coherence hypothesis on the source of the quotient (removable once
    87	extension-closure of quasi-coherence, Stacks 01LA, is available; see the
    88	declaration docstring), discharged here by `pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom` +
    89	`Modules.unit_isQuasicoherent` since the source is the pulled-back unit.
    90	The supporting lemmas — the Stacks 00HL algebra heart
    91	`Module.Flat.rTensor_injective_of_exact`, the comparison map
    92	`Modules.pullbackKernelComparison`, and the chart-shrinking lemmas — live in
    93	`Picard/FlatKernelBase.lean`; the derivation of the pinned statement from
    94	the isomorphism form of the comparison is
    95	`Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial_of_isIso_kernelComparison` (§0).
    96

    98	`Scheme.QuotFunctor` (`Modules.pullback_id_app_coherence`,
    99	`Modules.pullback_comp_app_coherence_inv`), which was stated in
   100	`QuotFunctorDef.lean` for arbitrary modules and so applies to the unit.

     9	/-!
    10	# The divisor-support quasi-finiteness binder, reduced to its geometric core
    11	
    12	`AJC.picrep.divlocallyclosed`.
    13	
    14	## The obligation this file is about
    15	
    16	`Picard/DivPushforwardFlat.lean` carries, on every one of its theorems, the instance
    17	binder
    18	
    19	```
    20	[LocallyQuasiFinite (schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)]
    21	```
    22	
    23	— "the divisor `D ⊆ X_T` has finite fibres over `T`" — and says of it, in its own
    24	module docstring, that it "has no producer in this project", that
    25	`LocallyQuasiFinite` "occurs nowhere else in `Picard/`", and that it is
    26	"kernel-checked NOT derivable from `DivFamily`'s other fields". All three
    27	statements are true at HEAD and none of them is weakened here.
    28	
    29	What *was* never measured is **how much of that binder is geometry**. This file
    30	measures it, and the answer is that the binder is one topological statement away
    31	from free: two of the three inputs the mathlib criteria want are supplied by
    32	`DivFamily.properSupport`, which every family already carries.
    33	
    34	## What is proved here
    35	
    36	* `Scheme.Modules.locallyOfFiniteType_schematicSupportι_comp` and
    37	  `Scheme.Modules.quasiCompact_schematicSupportι_comp` — from
    38	  `HasProperSupport` alone, the support map is locally of finite type and
    39	  quasi-compact. Both by synthesis once `IsProper` is in scope; recorded as named
    40	  theorems because `HasProperSupport` is a `def`, not a class, so a consumer
    41	  writing `haveI := hps` gets **no** instance and the synthesis silently fails
    42	  (measured: `infer_instance` fails on both goals with the `def` in scope and
    43	  succeeds with the `IsProper` restatement).
    44	
    45	* `Scheme.Modules.locallyQuasiFinite_schematicSupportι_comp_iff_finite_fibers` —
    46	  the binder **is equivalent** to finiteness of each set-theoretic fibre of the
    47	  divisor over the base, for an arbitrary module with proper support over an
    48	  arbitrary morphism. No curve, no smoothness, no relative dimension, no
    49	  `DivFamily`.
    50	
    51	* `Scheme.Modules.locallyQuasiFinite_schematicSupportι_comp_iff_isFinite_fiber` —
    52	  the same equivalence in the scheme-theoretic form, against
    53	  `IsFinite (…).fiberToSpecResidueField t`.
    54	
    55	* `Scheme.Modules.locallyQuasiFinite_schematicSupportι_comp_of_finite_fibers` —
    56	  the direction a producer needs, as a standalone implication.
    57	
    58	* `Scheme.DivFamily.locallyQuasiFinite_of_finite_fibers` and
    59	  `Scheme.DivFamily.locallyQuasiFinite_iff_finite_fibers` — the same statements
    60	  at a `DivFamily`, where `properSupport` is a field, so the hypothesis list is
    61	  *only* the fibre finiteness.
    62	
    63	* `Scheme.Modules.locallyQuasiFinite_schematicSupportι` — for contrast, and
    64	  because it is the fact that makes the composite's failure informative: the
    65	  support immersion **on its own** is always locally quasi-finite, for every
    66	  module on every scheme, by `IsPreimmersion`. So nothing about the annihilator
    67	  or the support is what the binder is asking for; the whole content sits in the
    68	  projection to `T`.
    69	
    70	## What this does NOT do, stated because it is the natural over-reading
    71	
    72	* It does **not** produce the binder for any family. The remaining obligation is
    73	  the fibre finiteness, and that is where relative dimension one enters: on the
    74	  curve fibre `C_t` the divisor `D_t` is the zero scheme of a regular section of
    75	  an invertible ideal (`Picard/DivDegree.lean` has that fibre short exact
    76	  sequence in full — `Scheme.DivFamily.isLocallyTrivial_fiber_kernel` (the bare
    77	  name fails `#check`: it lives in the `Scheme.DivFamily` namespace, not
    78	  `Scheme.Modules`), `mono_fiber_kernel_ι`,
    79	  `fiberKernelIso`, `fiberCokernelIso`), hence `0`-dimensional, hence finite. That
    80	  step is genuinely absent and is not attempted here.
    81	
    82	* It does **not** close `AJC.picrep.divlocallyclosed`. D3′ proper is the
    83	  `ExistsUnique` statement about the Grassmannian locus; this file is upstream of
    84	  it.
    85	
    86	* It does **not** inhabit `Scheme.DivFamily`. `Picard/DivFamilyZero.lean`'s
    87	  `DivFamily.zero` is the tree's only producer, so every statement here is
    88	  testable at exactly one family.
    89	
    90	* It closes **no** `sorry`, and `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` is untouched.
    91	  A shorter hypothesis list on the divisor side is not progress on the seam's
    92	  `rep`, and this file is verified with that theorem as a `sorryAx` control.
    93	
    94	## Why the reduction is worth landing separately
    95	
    96	The reduction is a repricing of D3′'s hypothesis: the binder is no longer an
    97	affine-local `RingHom.QuasiFinite` condition to be attacked at each site, but one
    98	fibre statement, with every scheme-level binder discharged from a field a family
    99	already carries.
   100	
   101	**"THREE ROWS" WAS AN OVERCOUNT AND IS WITHDRAWN — it is ONE row plus a partial
   102	contribution to a gate** (fresh-context audit, `I-1618`; the earlier text here, and
   103	this file's commit messages, said the reduction retires plumbing for D3′, D4′ and
   104	the local-constancy gate at once).
   105	
   106	* **D3′** — yes. This is that row's binder.
   107	* **D4′** — no. D4′ consumes D3′ and never binds `LocallyQuasiFinite` itself, so
   108	  counting it separately double-counts a single discharge.
   109	* **`Scheme.HasLocallyConstantDivDeg`** (`Picard/DivDegree.lean`) — partially. Its
   110	  own docstring names **two** inputs, "the finiteness/rank half of the campaign's
   111	  B3 rigid-pushforward engine **plus** relative-dimension-1 quasi-finiteness", and
   112	  its content is local constancy of a rank function. This file supplies at most the
   113	  second input.
   114	
   115	## References
   116	
   117	Blueprint: the campaign's D3′ node.
   118	Source: [Kleiman], "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §3 Def. `df:red`,
   119	Ex. `ex:DivC`. Mathlib: `AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/QuasiFinite.lean`
   120	(`locallyQuasiFinite_iff_finite_preimage_singleton`,
   121	`locallyQuasiFinite_iff_isFinite_fiber`,
   122	`LocallyQuasiFinite.of_finite_preimage_singleton`).
   123	-/

   139	/-! ## §1. The support immersion alone is always quasi-finite
   140	
   141	This section exists to locate the content of the binder. A reader pricing
   142	`LocallyQuasiFinite (schematicSupportι F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)` might expect the
   143	difficulty to be about the annihilator ideal sheaf or the schematic support, both
   144	of which are project-local primitives with a thin API
   145	(`Picard/QuotScheme.lean` records that `annihilator_ideal` itself is blocked on the
   146	QCoh localisation bridge). It is not: the support immersion is quasi-finite
   147	outright. -/
   148	
   149	/-- **The schematic-support immersion is always locally quasi-finite** — for every
   150	sheaf of modules on every scheme, with no hypothesis whatever.
   151	
   152	`schematicSupportι F` is `IdealSheafData.subschemeι` of the annihilator ideal
   153	sheaf, and mathlib registers `IsPreimmersion` for every `subschemeι`
   154	(`AlgebraicGeometry/IdealSheaf/Subscheme.lean`) together with a low-priority
   155	`IsPreimmersion ⟹ LocallyQuasiFinite` instance.
   156	
   157	**The `inferInstanceAs` is load-bearing and is not cosmetic**, and the mechanism is
   158	worth stating exactly, because two wrong versions of it have stood here. Measured,
   159	three spellings in one probe:
   160	
   161	* `LocallyQuasiFinite F.annihilator.subschemeι` — plain `infer_instance`
   162	  **succeeds**;
   163	* `LocallyQuasiFinite (schematicSupportι F)` — plain `infer_instance` **fails**;
   164	* the same after `unfold Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι` — still **fails**, and
   165	  `pp.explicit` shows why: the goal becomes
   166	  `@LocallyQuasiFinite (@schematicSupport X F) X (@IdealSheafData.subschemeι X
   167	  (@annihilator X F))`. Unfolding rewrote the **morphism** to the annihilator form
   168	  but left the **source scheme** as `schematicSupport X F`, so the instance —
   169	  indexed on `IdealSheafData.subscheme` as the source — does not apply.
   170	
   171	So the obstruction is the *source-object* index, not reducibility of the morphism,
   172	and it is not a missing instance: converting the goal wholesale with
   173	`inferInstanceAs` fixes it. (An earlier revision of this paragraph blamed
   174	"unfolding replaces the reducible definition by the `annihilator`-projection form
   175	that the instance is not indexed on", which has the direction backwards; a
   176	fresh-context audit then reported that the annihilator spelling *also* fails, which
   177	the first probe above refutes. Both are recorded because the two errors point
   178	opposite ways and a reader who inherits either will look in the wrong place.)
   179	Stated as a theorem so downstream sites cite a name rather than rediscover this. -/
   180	theorem locallyQuasiFinite_schematicSupportι (F : X.Modules) :
   181	    LocallyQuasiFinite (schematicSupportι F) :=
   182	  inferInstanceAs (LocallyQuasiFinite F.annihilator.subschemeι)
   183	
   184	/-- **The schematic-support immersion is a preimmersion**, hence injective on
   185	points. Same `inferInstanceAs` remark as above. Used below only through
   186	`Scheme.Hom.isEmbedding`. -/
   187	theorem isPreimmersion_schematicSupportι (F : X.Modules) :
   188	    IsPreimmersion (schematicSupportι F) :=
   189	  inferInstanceAs (IsPreimmersion F.annihilator.subschemeι)

   191	/-! ## §2. Two of the three inputs are free from `properSupport` -/
   192	
   193	section Composite
   194	
   195	variable {T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ T) (F : X.Modules)
   196	
   197	/-- **The support map is locally of finite type, from proper support alone.**
   198	
   199	`HasProperSupport f F` is by definition `IsProper (schematicSupportι F ≫ f)`
   200	(`Picard/QuotScheme.lean`), and mathlib derives `LocallyOfFiniteType` from
   201	`IsProper` by synthesis.
   202	
   203	**The restatement of the hypothesis as an `IsProper` instance is required.**
   204	`HasProperSupport` is a plain `def`, not a class, so `haveI := hps` registers
   205	nothing that instance search can use: `infer_instance` on this very goal
   206	**fails** with the `def` in scope and **succeeds** after
   207	`haveI : IsProper _ := hps` (measured both ways).
   208	
   209	**But the word "synthesis" overstates the step, and the gloss that stood here —
   210	that the failure "reads as *mathlib lacks `IsProper ⟹ LocallyOfFiniteType`*" — is
   211	withdrawn** (fresh-context audit, `I-1620`, reproduced by its author).
   212	`LocallyOfFiniteType` is a **structure parent** of `IsProper`, so this theorem is
   213	`hps.toLocallyOfFiniteType`: a field access, not an instance search, and no lemma
   214	is missing anywhere. `quasiCompact_schematicSupportι_comp` is one hop further
   215	(`hps.toUniversallyClosed`). The `def`-versus-class friction is real and worth a
   216	name; describing it as a synthesis gap sent the reader hunting a reducibility bug
   217	that does not exist. -/
   218	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_schematicSupportι_comp
   219	    (hps : HasProperSupport f F) :
   220	    LocallyOfFiniteType (schematicSupportι F ≫ f) :=
   221	  haveI : IsProper (schematicSupportι F ≫ f) := hps
   222	  inferInstance
   223	
   224	/-- **The support map is quasi-compact, from proper support alone.** Same route
   225	and same `def`-versus-class caveat as
   226	`locallyOfFiniteType_schematicSupportι_comp`. -/
   227	theorem quasiCompact_schematicSupportι_comp
   228	    (hps : HasProperSupport f F) :
   229	    QuasiCompact (schematicSupportι F ≫ f) :=
   230	  haveI : IsProper (schematicSupportι F ≫ f) := hps
   231	  inferInstance

   233	/-! ## §3. The binder is exactly the fibre finiteness -/
   234	
   235	/-- **The quasi-finiteness binder of the divisor side IS finiteness of the
   236	fibres**, for an arbitrary module with proper support over an arbitrary
   237	morphism of schemes.
   238	
   239	Both mathlib criteria that could give this want binders the caller does not
   240	obviously have: `locallyQuasiFinite_iff_finite_preimage_singleton` needs
   241	`LocallyOfFiniteType` *and* `QuasiCompact`. §2 supplies both from
   242	`HasProperSupport`, so the equivalence holds with **no** hypothesis beyond proper
   243	support.
   244	
   245	What this buys, and it is the point of the file: a lane producing the binder does
   246	not need to touch `LocallyQuasiFinite`, the annihilator ideal sheaf, the
   247	schematic support, or affine-local `RingHom.QuasiFinite` conditions at all. It
   248	needs one topological statement about the fibres of `D → T`. On a relative curve
   249	that statement is that a nonempty effective Cartier divisor on a `1`-dimensional
   250	fibre is a finite set of points — which is where the relative-dimension-one
   251	hypothesis genuinely enters, and it is *not* proved here. -/
   252	theorem locallyQuasiFinite_schematicSupportι_comp_iff_finite_fibers
   253	    (hps : HasProperSupport f F) :
   254	    LocallyQuasiFinite (schematicSupportι F ≫ f) ↔
   255	      ∀ t : T, ((schematicSupportι F ≫ f) ⁻¹' {t}).Finite :=
   256	  haveI : IsProper (schematicSupportι F ≫ f) := hps
   257	  locallyQuasiFinite_iff_finite_preimage_singleton
   258	
   259	/-- **The scheme-theoretic form of the same equivalence**: the binder holds iff
   260	every scheme-theoretic fibre of the divisor over the base is a finite scheme over
   261	the residue field.
   262	
   263	Stated alongside the point-set form because the two feed different producers. A
   264	route through the fibre short exact sequence of `Picard/DivDegree.lean`
   265	(`fiberCokernelIso`, which identifies `(O_D)_t` with the cokernel of the fibre
   266	ideal inclusion) lands naturally on *this* shape, since it produces a statement
   267	about the fibre as a scheme rather than about a preimage set. -/
   268	theorem locallyQuasiFinite_schematicSupportι_comp_iff_isFinite_fiber
   269	    (hps : HasProperSupport f F) :
   270	    LocallyQuasiFinite (schematicSupportι F ≫ f) ↔
   271	      ∀ t : T, IsFinite ((schematicSupportι F ≫ f).fiberToSpecResidueField t) :=
   272	  haveI : IsProper (schematicSupportι F ≫ f) := hps
   273	  locallyQuasiFinite_iff_isFinite_fiber
   274	
   275	/-- **The producer direction, standalone.** Given proper support, finiteness of
   276	the fibres *gives* the binder. Split out from the `iff` because a producer only
   277	ever uses this half, and because it is the form that lets a use site avoid
   278	naming `HasProperSupport` twice. -/
   279	theorem locallyQuasiFinite_schematicSupportι_comp_of_finite_fibers
   280	    (hps : HasProperSupport f F)
   281	    (hfib : ∀ t : T, ((schematicSupportι F ≫ f) ⁻¹' {t}).Finite) :
   282	    LocallyQuasiFinite (schematicSupportι F ≫ f) :=
   283	  haveI : IsProper (schematicSupportι F ≫ f) := hps
   284	  LocallyQuasiFinite.of_finite_preimage_singleton _ hfib
   285	
   286	/-- **A fibre of the divisor injects into the corresponding fibre of the ambient
   287	family.** The support immersion is a preimmersion, hence injective on points, and
   288	the fibre of the composite is by definition the preimage of the ambient fibre.
   289	
   290	Recorded because it is the shape in which the missing geometry will be consumed:
   291	it reduces fibre finiteness for `D → T` to finiteness of a *subset* of the curve
   292	fibre `C_t`, so a producer never has to reason about `D` as a scheme in its own
   293	right. Note the hypothesis is finiteness of the ambient fibre, which for a
   294	relative curve is **false** — so this lemma is a reduction tool for a cut-down
   295	subset, not a route to the binder by itself. -/
   296	theorem finite_fiber_schematicSupportι_comp_of_finite
   297	    {t : T} (hfin : (f ⁻¹' {t}).Finite) :
   298	    ((schematicSupportι F ≫ f) ⁻¹' {t}).Finite := by
   299	  haveI := isPreimmersion_schematicSupportι F
   300	  have hpre : ((schematicSupportι F ≫ f) ⁻¹' {t})
   301	      = (schematicSupportι F).base ⁻¹' (f ⁻¹' {t}) := rfl
   302	  rw [hpre]
   303	  exact hfin.preimage (schematicSupportι F).isEmbedding.injective.injOn
   304

   306	
   307	`LocallyQuasiFinite.of_fiberToSpecResidueField` reduces the binder to
   308	quasi-finiteness of each scheme-theoretic fibre of the divisor over the residue
   309	field of the base point, and it wants **neither** `LocallyOfFiniteType` **nor**
   310	`QuasiCompact`. So for an arbitrary module — no properness assumption whatever —
   311	this reduction has a shorter hypothesis list than
   312	`locallyQuasiFinite_schematicSupportι_comp_of_finite_fibers`.

   326	relative-curve geometry is fibrewise by nature (`D_t` is the zero scheme of a

   333	theorem locallyQuasiFinite_schematicSupportι_comp_of_fibers

   335	      ((schematicSupportι F ≫ f).fiberToSpecResidueField t)) :

   395	theorem locallyQuasiFinite_iff_finite_fibers (x : DivFamily π T) :

   399	  Modules.locallyQuasiFinite_schematicSupportι_comp_iff_finite_fibers _ _

   402	/-- **The scheme-theoretic form at a family.** Same content as
   403	`locallyQuasiFinite_iff_finite_fibers`, in the shape the fibre short exact

   405	theorem locallyQuasiFinite_iff_isFinite_fiber (x : DivFamily π T) :
   406	    LocallyQuasiFinite (Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom) ↔

    12	/-!
    13	# Representability of the relative Grassmannian (`thm:grassmannian_representable`)
    14	
    15	This file states and attacks the representability of the relative Grassmannian
    16	functor `Grass(V, d) : (Sch/S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type 1` (`Scheme.Grassmannian`,
    17	`QuotFunctorDef.lean`) by an `S`-scheme, for `V` a locally free
    18	`O_S`-module of rank `r` and `1 ≤ d ≤ r` ([Nitsure] §1, Exercise (2);
    19	blueprint `thm:grassmannian_representable`).
    20	
    21	The statement here **corrects** the earlier skeleton of `QuotFunctorDef.lean`,
    22	which quantified over an arbitrary sheaf of modules `V` with no rank data:
    23	that form is not the [Nitsure] theorem (whose hypotheses are `V` locally free
    24	of rank `r ≥ d ≥ 1`) and is not known to be true for non-quasi-coherent `V`.
    25	The universe is pinned to `Scheme.{0}`: the merged absolute chart construction
    26	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.scheme` / `.represents`,
    27	`GrassmannianQuot.lean`) lives over the genuinely terminal `Spec ℤ` of
    28	`Scheme.{0}`, and the relative theorem is obtained from it.
    29	
    30	## Contents
    31	
    32	* `Scheme.LocallyFreeQuotient.congrModule` / `Scheme.Grassmannian.congrIso` —
    33	  transport of the Grassmannian functor along an isomorphism `V ≅ V'` of the
    34	  classified module (pure functoriality, no pseudofunctor coherence).
    35	* `Scheme.LocallyFreeQuotient.toRankQuotient` / `.ofRankQuotient` /
    36	  `Scheme.Grassmannian.freeCompare` — for the free module `V = O_S^r`, the
    37	  comparison `Grass(O_S^r, d) ≅ (Over.forget S)ᵒᵖ ⋙ Grass(r, d)` with the
    38	  merged absolute Grassmannian functor, re-presenting the pulled-back free
    39	  module through `Scheme.Modules.pullbackFreeIso`.  Naturality is the free
    40	  coherence `pullbackFreeIso_comp` of `GlueDescent.lean`.
    41	* `Scheme.Grassmannian.prodRepresentableBy` — the absolute Grassmannian,
    42	  pulled back to `Over S` along the forgetful functor, is representable by
    43	  the product `S ⨯ Gr(d, r)` with its first projection (`Spec ℤ` is terminal
    44	  in `Scheme.{0}`, so the product is the base change of `Gr(d, r)` to `S`).
    45	* `Scheme.Grassmannian.representable_of_iso_free` — representability of
    46	  `Grass(V, d)` for globally trivialised `V ≅ O_S^r` (complete proof).
    47	* `Scheme.Grassmannian.representable` — the [Nitsure] statement, for `V`

   345	/-! ## §3. Representability of the pulled-back absolute functor
   346	
   347	`Scheme.{0}` has binary products (`Spec ℤ` is terminal, pullbacks exist), so
   348	the forgetful functor `Over S ⥤ Sch` has the right adjoint `Over.star S`,

+Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors

+import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivPushforwardFlat
+import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.GrassmannianRepresentability
+import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RigidPushforwardP1Sheaf
+
+/-!
+# The divisor-to-Grassmannian comparison
+
+This file begins campaign milestone D2': a divisor family is twisted by a fixed
+module on the curve, and the pullback--pushforward base-change map followed by
+the divisor quotient gives the canonical evaluation morphism used by the
+Grassmannian construction.
+
+The definitions in the first section are unconditional.  In particular,
+`DivFamily.grassmannianEval` exists before the Riemann--Roch argument proves it
+epimorphic.  Keeping the map separate from its eventual `Epi` proof prevents
+uniform generation from becoming an assumption in the definition of the
+comparison.
+
+The second section records two affine algebra bridges used to turn finite flat
+pushforwards into the rank-indexed local-freeness predicate expected by
+`Scheme.LocallyFreeQuotient`.  They do not introduce a representability gate:
+their inputs are ordinary finite-presentation, finiteness, and projectivity
+properties with producers elsewhere in the Picard development.
+-/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+
+universe u
+
+open CategoryTheory Limits
+
+namespace AlgebraicGeometry
+
+namespace Scheme
+
+namespace DivFamily
+
+variable {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} {T : Over S}
+
+/-- The twist of the divisor structure sheaf by a module on the original
+family.  For the D2' embedding, `L` is the chosen sufficiently positive
+projective twist. -/
+noncomputable def twist (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
+    (pullback π T.hom).Modules :=
+  Modules.tensorObj ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L) x.F
+
+/-- Tensor the divisor quotient `O -> O_D` with the pulled-back twist. -/
+noncomputable def twistQuotientMap (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
+    (Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L ⟶ x.twist L :=
+  (Modules.tensorObj_right_unitor _).inv ≫
+    Modules.tensorObj_functoriality (𝟙 _)
+      ((Modules.pullbackUnitIso (pullback.fst π T.hom)).inv ≫ x.q)
+
+/-- The canonical D2' evaluation morphism.
+
+It first base-changes `π_* L` from `S` to `T`, then pushes forward the twisted
+divisor quotient along `X_T -> T`.  Uniform Riemann--Roch will prove that this
+map is an epimorphism for a sufficiently positive `L`; no such conclusion is
+built into the definition. -/
+noncomputable def grassmannianEval (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
+    (Modules.pullback T.hom).obj ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) ⟶
+      (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L) :=
+  pushforwardBaseChangeMap π T.hom (pullback.snd π T.hom)
+      (pullback.fst π T.hom) pullback.condition L ≫
+    (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).map (x.twistQuotientMap L)
+
+end DivFamily
+
+namespace Modules
+
+/-- A finite global presentation of a module sheaf on `Spec R` induces a
+finite presentation of its module of global sections.

+global-section module, without any noetherian hypothesis on `R`. -/

+    {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (M : (Spec R).Modules) (P : M.Presentation)
+    [P.IsFinite] :
+    Module.FinitePresentation R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) := by
+  let g := (tilde.functor R).preimage <|
+    (tildeFinsupp _).hom ≫ P.relations.π ≫ kernel.ι _ ≫ (tildeFinsupp _).inv
+  let Q := (P.generators.I →₀ R) ⧸ LinearMap.range g.hom
+  have hQ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q := by
+    apply Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective
+      (Submodule.mkQ (LinearMap.range g.hom)) (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _)
+    rw [Submodule.ker_mkQ]
+    simpa only [LinearMap.range_eq_map] using Module.Finite.fg_top.map g.hom
+  let iso : cokernel ((tilde.functor R).map g) ≅
+      cokernel (P.relations.π ≫ kernel.ι _) := by
+    refine cokernel.mapIso _ _ (tildeFinsupp _) (tildeFinsupp _) ?_
+    simp only [g, (tilde.functor R).map_preimage]

+    PreservesCokernel.iso (tilde.functor R) g ≪≫ iso ≪≫
+      IsColimit.coconePointUniqueUpToIso (colimit.isColimit _) P.isColimit

+    (tilde.functor R).mapIso (ModuleCat.cokernelIsoRangeQuotient g).symm ≪≫ eC
